name: mnemonic_sonar_resonance
label: The Echo of Self
godotFeature: Godot's AudioServer, AudioStreamPlayer3D, Audio Busses with dynamic parameter control (e.g., volume, pitch, filter frequencies), and script-controlled audio effects for real-time sound manipulation.
poeticVision: The player will feel the terrifying intimacy of memory retrieval. As Lyra nears a memory fragment, a low, internal hum begins, growing in intensity and complexity — not external music, but the sound of her own subconscious mind grappling with a lost piece of self. When she touches it, a sudden, piercing *sonic flare* erupts, a raw, unfiltered snippet of a forgotten moment (a voice, a laugh, a scream, a specific environmental sound). This burst isn't just a reward; it's a *beacon*. The Silence hears it, drawn to the powerful resonance. The player experiences the harrowing truth: every step towards identity is a step closer to being caught, making 'remembering' a desperate, dangerous gamble.
usage: Attach this script to your player character (Lyra). In Godot's Project Settings -> Audio -> Buses, create two new Audio Buses: "HumBus" and "FlareBus". On "HumBus", add an `AudioEffectFilterBiquad` (or similar filter effect). On "FlareBus", add `AudioEffectDistortion` and `AudioEffectReverb` (and optionally an `AudioEffectFilterBiquad` if desired). Create `Node3D`s in your scene to represent memory fragments. For each `Node3D` fragment, add it to the "memory_fragments" group and set a `metadata` entry named `memory_audio_stream` with an `AudioStream` resource (e.g., `AudioStreamWAV`) containing the specific memory snippet. Ensure your `InputMap` has an action named "interact" (or change the `interaction_action` export variable). The script will automatically detect nearby fragments, modulate the "HumBus" based on proximity, and trigger a "sonic flare" on the "FlareBus" when a fragment is activated, emitting a `hunter_alert` signal.

parameters.name: hum_bus_name
parameters.description: The name of the AudioBus used for the internal hum effect.

parameters.name: flare_bus_name
parameters.description: The name of the AudioBus used for the sonic flare effect.

parameters.name: max_hum_distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance from a memory fragment at which the internal hum is audible.

parameters.name: min_hum_cutoff
parameters.description: The filter cutoff frequency for the hum bus at minimum hum intensity (far from fragment).

parameters.name: max_hum_cutoff
parameters.description: The filter cutoff frequency for the hum bus at maximum hum intensity (close to fragment).

parameters.name: flare_duration
parameters.description: The duration (in seconds) for which the extreme audio effects on the FlareBus are active after a memory is triggered.

parameters.name: flare_volume_boost
parameters.description: The additional volume (in dB) applied to the FlareBus during a sonic flare.

parameters.name: hunter_alert_radius
parameters.description: The radius around the activated memory fragment within which hunters are alerted.

parameters.name: interaction_distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance from a memory fragment at which Lyra can activate it.

parameters.name: interaction_action
parameters.description: The name of the input action used to activate a memory fragment.

verdict: To remember is to be found, a desperate symphony of self-reclamation echoing through the void, drawing the hunter ever closer.
impact: This invention fundamentally transforms memory retrieval from a simple objective into a harrowing, high-stakes gamble. Players will experience a constant, internal dread as they approach fragments, knowing that every step towards self-discovery is a broadcast to their relentless hunters. The visceral audio feedback creates an intimate connection to Lyra's dissolving identity, making the act of remembering a moment of both profound relief and terrifying vulnerability, forcing players to weigh the cost of regaining who they are against the immediate threat of annihilation.
